title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude partial outage 29 Sep hit Claude, Claude Code, Cowork and the API — fifth partial outage this month
bullets.summary: Errors began at 14:00 UTC (10:00 ET) and were mitigated by 14:36 UTC, with sign-in (SSO, Sign in with Apple), new chats and new Claude Code/Cowork sessions failing for a period; 12,000+ Downdetector reports. Earlier partial outages hit on 3, 11, 15 and 22 September.
bullets.how: The Construct: any Cowork scheduled task that fired in that window (10:00–10:40 ET) likely died silently — check the 29 Sep runs and add a retry-once rule plus a 'did it write today's file' check to each daily job. PRAGMA: single-vendor model dependency is a real client risk worth naming.

bullets.title: Anthropic's IPO prospectus leaks: $2T+ November listing target, ~80 of 261 pages on risk
bullets.summary: 29 Sep: reports on the leaked S-1 show an $8B+ operating loss on $4.6B revenue for the reported period, Q2 2026 revenue of $11.5B with a second straight quarter of operating profit, and a November IPO targeting a $2T+ valuation; the filing warns of 'catastrophic or existential risk'.
bullets.how: The Construct runs almost entirely on Claude: a public Anthropic means quarterly disclosure on pricing, capacity and reliability we can plan around. PRAGMA: the risk-factor section is ready-made material for client conversations about vendor concentration.

bullets.title: Informa TechTarget puts its person-level B2B buyer-intent data behind an MCP server (30 Sep)
bullets.summary: TechTarget's Buyer Intelligence (intent signals, pain points, persona/ICP data) is now callable from Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini and custom agents to build account battlecards and personalized outreach inside the AI workflow.
bullets.how: PRAGMA: the intent-data vendors are moving into the agent; an outbound/battlecard agent for PRAGMA's own pipeline becomes a connector, not a build. Brand 9 Signs: low fit (TechTarget's audience is tech buyers, not homebuilders).

bullets.title: Docusign opens its MCP server to every AI agent today (30 Sep)
bullets.summary: Docusign's MCP server, backed by its Iris AI engine, becomes callable from Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Slack and any MCP client, with account-level admin controls and access to past negotiations, clauses and policy across its agreement suite.
bullets.how: Brand 9 Signs: proposal-to-signature for Lennar/builder jobs could run from the agent (draft, send, track signed status into Atlas). The Construct already lists a Docusign plugin connector that needs authorization; wire it only if B9 signs enough contracts in Docusign to justify it.

bullets.title: Reco raises $55M to discover AI agents and track their apps, accounts and permissions
bullets.summary: 29 Sep: agent-security startup Reco raised $55M (total $140M) and expanded its platform to inventory AI agents across 280+ apps, as TechCrunch notes the agent-security category is getting crowded.
bullets.how: PRAGMA: 'which agents do you run and what can each one touch' is becoming a funded category — an agent inventory + permissions map is a sellable first deliverable. The Construct: we should hold that same map for Hermes, launchd jobs and Cowork tasks ourselves.

praxis_lesson: Claude went partly down for 36 minutes on a weekday morning, the fifth time this month. A scheduled job that fails once and never retries is a gap on the dashboard nobody notices; every daily Construct job should retry once and confirm its output file exists.
